A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffusionFF study and include readable supplementary material. Their methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite extensive rewriting and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection and DSSIM localization results, architectural ablations and supplementary training experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds corruption tests, DFDC localization examples and DDPM/DDIM sampling comparisons.

M1.justification: The pretrained detector, multi-scale U-Net conditioning, gated fusion and two-stage MSE/CE training remain unchanged. The encoder/decoder terminology and Equation 5 describe the existing design. The DDPM equation correction does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: The same FF++, CDF2, DFDC, DFDCP and FFIW datasets remain. V2 adds controlled JPEG compression, occlusion, Gaussian noise and blur scenarios on CDF2, extending input-condition coverage without introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces LESB with reproduced Effort results; the other main benchmark comparators remain. V2 additionally compares against SBI in the new corruption experiment and against DDIM in the sampling analysis.

E3.justification: Main benchmark protocols remain unchanged. V2 specifies three severity levels per corruption and replaces the timestep study at T=40/50/75/100 with DDPM evaluations at T=20/50/100/500/1000 and DDIM sampling budgets using a T=1000 model. This study now reports SSIM alone instead of four localization metrics.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the analyses with a four-degradation robustness study (Figure 7), qualitative DFDC localization comparisons (Figure 8), and a broader timestep study including DDIM (Figure 9). These address additional robustness and sampling-design questions. Existing architecture, fusion, detector, seed and two-stage training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The same qualitative comparison across three denoising seeds remains, moving from v1 Figure 7 to v2 Figure 10. V2 adds no repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Substantial new corruption, sampling and DFDC qualitative results accompany unchanged main DiffusionFF scores and Tables 2–7. Effort's added results narrow the reported lead to 0.27 AUC points on DFDC and 0.03 on FFIW. Figure 7 newly reports, for example, 74.86% versus SBI's 57.10% under severe occlusion. Figure 9 reports a T=20 result despite v1 stating non-convergence for T<=30; the earlier four-metric timestep results are partly removed.

T1.justification: Equation 4 is mathematically corrected: v1's deterministic clean-sample rescaling becomes a DDPM reverse update with different coefficients and an explicit Gaussian variance term. V2 also defines the noise-schedule quantities explicitly. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim fine-grained diffusion-based DSSIM localization, improved detection through feature fusion, and state-of-the-art performance with greater explainability. V2's joint-task title and artifact encoder/decoder framing recast the same contributions without establishing a new capability or broader scientific claim.

C2.justification: Sections 8.3–8.4 add an explanation of the previously reported training collapse through all-black outputs and explicitly acknowledge slow inference and inapplicability to entirely synthesized images. V2 also replaces v1's multi-metric quality/efficiency tradeoff for T=50 with a task-specific explanation of its SSIM optimum.

D1.justification: Section 6.4 newly discloses ConvNeXt-B pretraining: 200 epochs, AdamW, batch size 64, learning rate 5e-5 and linear decay from epoch 100. These are additional disclosures, not established setting changes. Conversely, Figure 3 replaces the explicit GAP/Norm/Linear classifier details with a generic Head.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Effort, DDIM, WMamba and UCF, while removing LESB. It also removes v1's criticisms that DiffForensics overuses diffusion and DiffusionFake struggles with unseen identities, instead positioning fine-grained artifact localization as an underexplored application. The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation and method explanations are extensively rewritten around joint detection/localization and artifact encoder/decoder terminology. V2 introduces a detailed numbered section hierarchy, reorganizes the analyses and supplement, and revises the title and author information.

P2.justification: V2 extensively reformats the title block, typography, table captions and placement of figures and tables. It adds robustness and DFDC visualizations, replaces the timestep table with DDPM/DDIM plots, and simplifies the architecture diagram's classifier display. Existing seed examples and training-strategy results are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through corruption and sampling comparisons, corrects the DDPM equation, and improves reproducibility and scope clarity through pretraining details and explicit limitations. These gains are moderated by replacing v1's multi-metric timestep evidence with SSIM alone and leaving the new T=20 result inconsistent with v1's non-convergence statement. The net improvement is useful but limited.
